page.title: Sotogrande Yacht Charter Fishing Trip: Species & Seasons

faq.q: Can I fish from any of your boats?
faq.a: Yes, all our boats are suitable for rod fishing. The skipper will advise on the best spots. For serious trolling, we recommend the Mangusta 80 (24m) or Azimut 58 Flybridge for their speed and deck space.

faq.q: What is the best time of year for bluefin tuna?
faq.a: Bluefin tuna are most common from June to September when sea temperatures reach 22–28°C. July and August offer the highest catch rates. We recommend a full-day charter (8 hours) to maximise your chances.

faq.q: How far is Sotogrande from Puerto Banús?
faq.a: Sotogrande is about 20 nautical miles south of Puerto Banús. By powerboat at 25–30 knots, it takes roughly 45 minutes. Our boats depart from Puerto Banús, so factor this travel time into your charter.

faq.q: Can I keep the fish I catch?
faq.a: Yes, you may keep legal-sized fish within Spanish regulations. The skipper will advise on size limits and bag limits. Many guests choose catch-and-release, especially for bluefin tuna. We can help with cleaning if needed.

faq.q: What other fish can I catch near Sotogrande?
faq.a: Common catches include seabass, sea bream, amberjack, mackerel, and bonito. In deeper waters off Cabo de Gata, you may also find dentex and grouper. The variety is excellent from spring through autumn.
No separate licence is needed for recreational fishing on a charter boat with a licensed skipper. The boat's insurance covers all passengers. Just bring your own rod or rent one locally.

faq.q: What is the minimum charter duration for fishing?
faq.a: We recommend at least 6 hours to reach productive grounds and have enough fishing time. An 8-hour charter gives you the best chance, especially for tuna. Half-day (4h) trips are possible but limited to inshore areas.

data.body_html:
A sotogrande yacht charter fishing trip is one of the most rewarding ways to experience the Costa del Sol’s rich marine life. While Sotogrande itself is a prestigious marina, our fleet departs from Puerto Banús, just 20 nautical miles north — a 45-minute cruise south along the coast. Whether you’re after bluefin tuna, seabass, or sea bream, the waters off Sotogrande offer excellent fishing from spring through autumn. Here’s what you need to know about species, seasons, and booking the right boat.

Why fish near Sotogrande?

Sotogrande sits at the mouth of the Guadiaro River, where freshwater meets the Mediterranean. This nutrient-rich zone attracts baitfish, which in turn draw larger predators. The seabed drops quickly to 50–100 metres just a few miles offshore, creating ideal conditions for trolling and bottom fishing. Unlike the crowded beaches of Marbella, the waters off Sotogrande are quieter, with less boat traffic and clearer water. For a sotogrande yacht charter fishing trip, you’ll want a boat that can cover the distance comfortably and give you deck space to fight fish.

Our recommended boats for fishing

All our charters include a licensed skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, and insurance. For fishing, we suggest boats with speed and space. The Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) from €4,719 for 4 hours includes a free jet ski — perfect for families who want both fishing and water sports. The Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax) offers a large cockpit and flybridge for spotting fish. For smaller groups, the Pershing 46 (14m, 10 pax) is fast and nimble. All depart from Puerto Banús. For a full list, see our boat rental Marbella fleet.

Species by season

The Mediterranean off Sotogrande hosts a variety of game fish. Here’s a seasonal breakdown:

  • Spring (March–May): Seabass and sea bream are abundant inshore. Water temps 15–20°C. Good for light tackle fishing.
  • Summer (June–September): Bluefin tuna arrive, often in schools. Water temps 22–28°C. Trolling with lures is most effective. Also bonito and mackerel.
  • Autumn (October–November): Seabass return as waters cool. Amberjack and dentex are possible in deeper areas. Water temps 18–22°C.
  • Winter (December–February): Slower fishing, but hake and red mullet can be caught. Most charters run year-round.

For a serious sotogrande yacht charter fishing trip, target June–September for tuna or March–May for seabass. Check our best time to charter a boat in Marbella guide for more detail.

What’s included in your charter

Every booking includes a licensed skipper who knows the local waters, fuel for the day, and a selection of drinks (water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava) plus light snacks. Insurance and safety equipment are covered. Spanish IVA (21%) is included in all prices. Fishing gear is not provided, but you can bring your own rods and tackle. The skipper will help with rigging and recommend bait. For larger groups, the Ferretti 94 (29m, 12 pax) offers luxury and space, but pricing is on request.

Planning your trip: distance and timing

From Puerto Banús to Sotogrande is roughly 20 nautical miles. At 25 knots, that’s 45 minutes each way. For a full fishing day, we recommend an 8-hour charter (€2,299 for Tier A boats, or Tier B from €4,719/4h). A 6-hour trip gives you about 4 hours of actual fishing time. Half-day (4h) options are available but limit you to inshore grounds near Cabopino or Cala del Faro. Always factor in travel time when booking. Our skippers will suggest the best route based on conditions and target species.

Where to fish near Sotogrande

Popular fishing grounds include the area off Cabo de Gata (rocky reefs), the Guadiaro River mouth (seabass), and deeper waters south of Estepona (tuna). The coastline between Puerto Banús and Sotogrande offers varied underwater topography — sand flats, seagrass meadows, and rocky outcrops. Your skipper will adjust based on wind and tide. For a truly memorable day, combine fishing with a stop at Cala Cortés for a swim and lunch. See our Marbella boat charter itineraries for route ideas.

Frequently asked questions

Can I fish from any of your boats?

Yes, all our boats are suitable for rod fishing. The skipper will advise on the best spots. For serious trolling, we recommend the Mangusta 80 (24m) or Azimut 58 Flybridge for their speed and deck space.

Do you provide fishing equipment?

We do not supply rods or tackle as standard. You are welcome to bring your own gear. The skipper can help with rigging and bait. If you need rental equipment, please ask when booking and we can arrange it locally.

What is the best time of year for bluefin tuna?

Bluefin tuna are most common from June to September when sea temperatures reach 22–28°C. July and August offer the highest catch rates. We recommend a full-day charter (8 hours) to maximise your chances.

How far is Sotogrande from Puerto Banús?

Sotogrande is about 20 nautical miles south of Puerto Banús. By powerboat at 25–30 knots, it takes roughly 45 minutes. Our boats depart from Puerto Banús, so factor this travel time into your charter.

Can I keep the fish I catch?

Yes, you may keep legal-sized fish within Spanish regulations. The skipper will advise on size limits and bag limits. Many guests choose catch-and-release, especially for bluefin tuna. We can help with cleaning if needed.

What other fish can I catch near Sotogrande?

Common catches include seabass, sea bream, amberjack, mackerel, and bonito. In deeper waters off Cabo de Gata, you may also find dentex and grouper. The variety is excellent from spring through autumn.

Is a fishing licence required?

No separate licence is needed for recreational fishing on a charter boat with a licensed skipper. The boat's insurance covers all passengers. Just bring your own rod or rent one locally.

What is the minimum charter duration for fishing?

We recommend at least 6 hours to reach productive grounds and have enough fishing time. An 8-hour charter gives you the best chance, especially for tuna. Half-day (4h) trips are possible but limited to inshore areas.
